title: WebCoder: Scaling General Frontend Development with Artifact-Grounded Agentic Reinforcement Learning
title_zh: WebCoder：基于工件导向的智能体强化学习扩展通用前端开发

paragraphs.en: Real-world frontend development requires agents to compose reproduction, generation, modification, and repair over an evolving application state. Learning a general policy for this process requires translating heterogeneous execution feedback into task-aligned rewards and effective credit assignment across long sequences of interdependent actions. We introduce WebCoder , a general frontend development agent trained with artifact-grounded agentic reinforcement learning. Our key idea is to assess diverse development activities through their effects on a shared executable artifact and its satisfaction of task requirements. We build Webdev-World, an executable environment that integrates code editing, application execution, browser inspection, and on-demand skills while preserving project state across interactions. An independent verifier evaluates the final application against task requirements to provide terminal rewards, while changes in intermediate artifact progress redistribute the resulting rollout advantage across development segments. Context compaction and message-tree sample construction support training on trajectories beyond a single context window while avoiding repeated loss computation on shared generated history. We further introduce Webdev-Bench to evaluate composed development requirements within a single project. On Webdev-Bench, WebCoder-27B raises requirement satisfaction from 64.8 for its Qwen3.8-27B base model to 72.8, exceeding Claude-Opus-4.8 (65.1) and GPT-5.4 (59.6); on Vision2Web, it improves the average visual and functional score from 41.1 to 62.4, on par with Claude-Opus-4.8. Ablation studies confirm the contributions of artifact-grounded credit assignment and long-horizon training.
paragraphs.zh: 真实世界的前端开发要求智能体在不断演进的应用状态上进行复现、生成、修改和修复的组合操作。 为这一过程学习一个通用策略，需要将异构的执行反馈转化为与任务对齐的奖励，并在长序列的相互依赖动作之间进行有效的信用分配。 我们提出 WebCoder，一个通过基于产物的智能体强化学习训练的通用前端开发智能体。 我们的核心思想是，通过多样的开发活动对共享可执行产物的影响及其对任务要求的满足程度来评估这些活动。 我们构建了 Webdev-World，一个可执行环境，它集成了代码编辑、应用执行、浏览器检查和按需技能，同时在交互过程中保留项目状态。 一个独立的验证器根据任务要求评估最终应用以提供终止奖励，而中间产物进展的变化则将由此产生的 rollout 优势重新分配到各开发片段上。 上下文压缩和消息树样本构建支持在超出单个上下文窗口的轨迹上进行训练，同时避免对共享的已生成历史进行重复的损失计算。 我们进一步提出 Webdev-Bench，用于在单个项目内评估组合式开发要求。 在 Webdev-Bench 上，WebCoder-27B 将要求满足度从其基座模型 Qwen3.8-27B 的 64.8 提升到 72.8，超过了 Claude-Opus-4.8（65.1）和 GPT-5.4（59.6）；在 Vision2Web 上，它将平均视觉与功能得分从 41.1 提升到 62.4，与 Claude-Opus-4.8 相当。 消融研究证实了基于产物的信用分配和长时程训练的贡献。

paragraphs.en: Recent advances in multimodal code generation have expanded the capabilities of frontend agents, from reproducing webpage designs ( Si et al., 2025 ; Xu et al., 2025 ; Xu et al., 2026 ) to refining interfaces through rendered feedback ( Yang et al., 2026 ; Deng et al., 2026 ) and generating interactive websites ( Lu et al., 2026 ) . In practice, these capabilities often need to work together within the same application. A user may ask an agent to reproduce a reference design, add a product section, connect it to an existing shopping cart, and preserve the navigation behavior. These requirements share code and application state: implementing a new feature can affect the layout, while a visual revision can disrupt an existing interaction. As illustrated in Figure 1 , completing such a request requires reproduction, generation, modification, and repair to be coordinated throughout development. This raises a central question: how can we train a general frontend agent to compose these capabilities over an evolving application state?
paragraphs.zh: 多模态代码生成的最新进展拓展了前端智能体的能力，从复现网页设计（Si et al., 2025；Xu et al., 2025；Xu et al., 2026），到通过渲染反馈优化界面（Yang et al., 2026；Deng et al., 2026），再到生成交互式网站（Lu et al., 2026）。 在实践中，这些能力往往需要在同一个应用内协同工作。 用户可能要求智能体复现一个参考设计，添加一个产品板块，将其连接到现有的购物车，并保持导航行为不变。 这些需求共享代码与应用状态：实现新功能可能影响布局，而视觉上的修改可能破坏已有的交互。 如图 1 所示，完成这样一个请求需要在整个开发过程中协调复现、生成、修改与修复。 这引出了一个核心问题：我们如何训练一个通用的前端智能体，使其能够在不断演进的应用状态之上组合这些能力？

paragraphs.en: Training such an agent requires coordinating activities whose local goals differ but whose effects are coupled through shared code and application state. Satisfying one requirement can violate another, making it necessary to assess the combined effects of these activities on the application. Progress may become observable only after several edits and executions, while later changes can introduce regressions, making it difficult to distinguish the contributions of different development stages. The interaction history can also outgrow the model’s context window as the project evolves. Therefore, learning a general policy requires a common basis for evaluating heterogeneous activities, credit assignment across interdependent stages, and support for long-horizon training.
paragraphs.zh: 训练这样的智能体需要协调多个活动，这些活动的局部目标各不相同，但其效果通过共享代码和应用状态相互耦合。 满足一项需求可能会违反另一项需求，因此有必要评估这些活动对应用的综合影响。 进展可能只有在多次编辑和执行之后才能显现出来，而后期的更改又可能引入回归问题，这使得难以区分不同开发阶段各自的贡献。 随着项目的演进，交互历史也可能超出模型的上下文窗口。 因此，学习一个通用策略需要一个评估异构活动的共同基础、跨相互依赖阶段的信用分配，以及对长时程训练的支持。

paragraphs.en: To address these challenges, we introduce WebCoder , a general frontend development agent trained with artifact-grounded agentic reinforcement learning . We unify heterogeneous frontend tasks within Webdev-World , an executable environment that provides a shared, task-agnostic interface for code editing, execution, browser inspection, and on-demand skills while preserving project state across interactions. This common interaction space allows a single policy to interleave reproduction, generation, modification, and repair as the application evolves. Our key idea is to ground policy learning in the evolution of an executable application, using task requirements to evaluate both the final outcome and intermediate development progress. Evaluating build results, rendered pages, and interaction outcomes against the same requirements provides a common basis for assessing the combined effects of development activities and optimizing the policy from its own trajectories.
paragraphs.zh: 为应对这些挑战，我们提出了 WebCoder，一个通过基于产物的智能体强化学习训练的通用前端开发智能体。 我们将异构的前端任务统一到 Webdev-World 中，这是一个可执行环境，为代码编辑、执行、浏览器检查和按需技能提供共享的、与任务无关的接口，同时在交互过程中保留项目状态。 这个共同的交互空间使单一策略能够在应用演进过程中交替执行复现、生成、修改和修复。 我们的核心思想是将策略学习锚定在可执行应用的演进上，利用任务需求来评估最终结果和中间开发进展。 基于相同需求评估构建结果、渲染页面和交互结果，为评估开发活动的综合效果以及从策略自身的轨迹中优化策略提供了共同基础。

paragraphs.en: Specifically, we construct a weighted checklist from the task requirements and use an independent verifier to build, run, and inspect the final application. Deterministic checks and visual assessments measure requirement satisfaction, with the aggregated score gated by successful execution and rendering to form the terminal reward. This terminal reward evaluates the final outcome but does not distinguish which development stages advanced the task or introduced regressions. Thus, we estimate intermediate requirement satisfaction from available project and execution evidence using the same checklist. Changes in these estimates provide stage-level progress and regression signals, which guide credit assignment across the trajectory and help the policy learn from the development process. For training across context windows, we combine context compaction with message-tree sample construction. Compaction lets development continue while project state persists in Webdev-World. A message tree records histories across context rewrites, enabling training on different stages of the same trajectory. Shared generated history remains available as context but contributes to the policy loss at most once.
paragraphs.zh: 具体而言，我们根据任务需求构建一个加权检查表，并使用独立的验证器来构建、运行和检查最终的应用程序。 确定性检查与视觉评估用于衡量需求的满足程度，其聚合得分以成功执行和渲染为门控条件，从而形成终局奖励。 该终局奖励评估的是最终结果，但无法区分是哪些开发阶段推进了任务或引入了回归。 因此，我们使用同一检查表，从可获取的项目和执行证据中估计中间阶段的需求满足程度。 这些估计值的变化提供了阶段级别的进度与回归信号，用于指导轨迹中的信用分配，并帮助策略从开发过程中学习。 为了跨上下文窗口进行训练，我们将上下文压缩与消息树样本构建相结合。 压缩使开发得以继续进行，同时项目状态持续保存在 Webdev-World 中。 消息树记录了上下文重写之间的历史，使得能够在同一轨迹的不同阶段上进行训练。 共享的生成历史仍可作为上下文使用，但对策略损失的贡献至多计算一次。

paragraphs.en: Our main contributions are summarized as follows:
paragraphs.zh: 我们的主要贡献总结如下：

paragraphs.en: We study general frontend development as capability composition over a persistent project state, and introduce Webdev-World as a shared environment for training WebCoder , a general frontend development agent.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将通用前端开发研究为基于持久项目状态的能力组合，并介绍 Webdev-World 作为一个共享环境，用于训练通用前端开发智能体 WebCoder。

paragraphs.en: We develop artifact-grounded agentic reinforcement learning , using task requirements to connect final application verification with progress-based credit assignment, and supporting training over trajectories that span multiple context windows.

paragraphs.en: We introduce Webdev-Bench to assess capability composition and preservation of specified existing behavior, and demonstrate improved visual and functional performance on Vision2Web.

paragraphs.en: We present an artifact-grounded agentic reinforcement learning framework for training WebCoder to compose frontend development capabilities over a persistent project state (Figure 2 ). We formulate the task, introduce Webdev-World as the shared environment, describe how one requirement decomposition connects terminal rewards with progress-based credit assignment, and detail training on trajectories that span multiple context windows.

paragraphs.en: Webdev-World is an executable environment with a common interface for code editing, command execution, browser inspection, and on-demand skills. Each rollout runs in an isolated container initialized with a React/Vite scaffold or an existing project, and project files persist across interactions, so a single policy can interleave development activities over the same evolving application. The policy edits the repository through file and shell tools and invokes webshot to build and serve the application and obtain rendered screenshots and DOM statistics, which show how preceding changes affect the application; on-demand skills provide procedural guidance for page decomposition, asset preparation, code generation, validation, and repair.
paragraphs.zh: Webdev-World 是一个可执行环境，为代码编辑、命令执行、浏览器检查以及按需技能提供统一接口。 每次 rollout 都在一个隔离容器中运行，容器以 React/Vite 脚手架或现有项目初始化，并且项目文件在多次交互之间持久保存，因此单个策略可以在同一个不断演进的应用上交替开展开发活动。 该策略通过文件和 shell 工具编辑代码仓库，并调用 webshot 来构建和运行应用、获取渲染截图与 DOM 统计信息，这些信息展示了此前的更改如何影响应用；按需技能为页面分解、资源准备、代码生成、验证与修复提供流程性指导。

paragraphs.en: The terminal reward measures task completion in the final project but does not directly distinguish the contributions of different stages in a long development trajectory. Thus, we estimate intermediate requirement satisfaction using the same checklist as final verification and use changes in these estimates to adjust stage-level advantages. The effect of a code change becomes observable only after the application is built, run, and inspected, so progress cannot be attributed to individual tool calls. We therefore assign credit at the level of segments, taking context compaction boundaries as natural segment boundaries, and measure progress by the change in project state between consecutive boundaries.
paragraphs.zh: 终端奖励衡量的是最终项目中的任务完成情况，但无法直接区分漫长开发轨迹中不同阶段的贡献。 因此，我们使用与最终验证相同的检查清单来估计中间需求满足程度，并利用这些估计值的变化来调整阶段级优势。 代码变更的效果只有在应用被构建、运行和检查之后才能显现，因此进展无法归因于单个工具调用。 为此，我们在片段层级上分配信用，将上下文压缩边界作为自然的片段边界，并通过相邻边界之间项目状态的变化来衡量进展。

paragraphs.en: Table 1 reports the main results. On Webdev-Bench, WebCoder-27B reaches an RS of 72.8, above the base model Qwen3.8-27B (64.8) and the strongest baseline Claude-Opus-4.8 (65.1); the remaining proprietary models lie between 48.0 and 59.6. paragraphs.en: We compare the full model with two ablated variants that share its initialization, training data, terminal reward, and hyperparameters, evaluated on Vision2Web L2 with the base model as reference. w/o Compaction (linear truncation) treats each rollout as a single linear token sequence and trains only on its first 65,536 tokens. w/o Artifact-Grounded Credit Assignment keeps the sample-construction procedure but gives all segments of a rollout the same rollout-level GRPO advantage.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将完整模型与两个消融变体进行比较，这些变体共享相同的初始化、训练数据、终端奖励和超参数，并在 Vision2Web L2 上以基础模型作为参考进行评估。w/o Compaction（线性截断）将每次轨迹展开（rollout）视为单个线性 token 序列，并且仅在其前 65,536 个 token 上进行训练。w/o Artifact-Grounded Credit Assignment 保留样本构建流程，但为一次轨迹展开的所有片段赋予相同的轨迹展开级 GRPO 优势。

paragraphs.en: Figure 4 reports evaluation scores on a fixed held-out set of 28 anchor tasks and rewards from on-policy training rollouts; the fixed set gives a common reference across checkpoints, whereas training rewards depend on the tasks sampled at each step. The anchor score increases across all evaluated checkpoints, from 0.346 at step 4 to 0.575 at step 29 (a relative gain of 66.2%), with improvements within both training stages. paragraphs.en: Automated frontend development spans reproducing interfaces from visual references, generating applications from textual requirements, and modifying or repairing existing projects. Datasets such as WebSight ( Laurençon et al., 2024 ) , Web2Code ( Yun et al., 2024 ) , and WebCode2M ( Gui et al., 2025a ) support screenshot-to-code learning, and benchmarks including Design2Code ( Si et al., 2025 ) , Sketch2Code ( Li et al., 2025 ) , Figma2Code ( Gui et al., 2026 ) , and Interaction2Code ( Xiao et al., 2025a ) evaluate generation from screenshots, sketches, design files, and interactive prototypes. WebGen-Bench ( Lu et al., 2025 ) and Vision2Web ( He et al., 2026 ) add browser-based functional testing, while DesignBench ( Xiao et al., 2025b ) and MT-Web2Code ( Li et al., 2026a ) cover editing and repair with preservation of unaffected content. On the modeling side, UICopilot ( Gui et al., 2025b ) and ScreenCoder ( Jiang et al., 2025 ) generate code coarse-to-fine, JanusCoder ( Sun et al., 2026 ) unifies generation and editing, UI2Code N ( Yang et al., 2026 ) and VisRefiner ( Deng et al., 2026 ) refine from rendered feedback, and WebWorld ( Xiao et al., 2026 ) selects browser-verified transitions for supervised training. Our work instead trains a single policy to compose all four activities within the same evolving application through artifact-grounded agentic reinforcement learning.
paragraphs.zh: 自动化前端开发包括从视觉参考复现界面、根据文本需求生成应用，以及对现有项目进行修改或修复。 WebSight（Laurençon 等，2024）、Web2Code（Yun 等，2024）和 WebCode2M（Gui 等，2025a）等数据集支持截图到代码的学习，而 Design2Code（Si 等，2025）、Sketch2Code（Li 等，2025）、Figma2Code（Gui 等，2026）和 Interaction2Code（Xiao 等，2025a）等基准则评估从截图、草图、设计文件和交互原型的生成。 WebGen-Bench（Lu 等，2025）和 Vision2Web（He 等，2026）增加了基于浏览器的功能测试，而 DesignBench（Xiao 等，2025b）和 MT-Web2Code（Li 等，2026a）则涵盖在保留未受影响内容前提下的编辑与修复。 在建模方面，UICopilot（Gui 等，2025b）和 ScreenCoder（Jiang 等，2025）以由粗到细的方式生成代码，JanusCoder（Sun 等，2026）统一了生成与编辑，UI2Code N（Yang 等，2026）和 VisRefiner（Deng 等，2026）基于渲染反馈进行优化，WebWorld（Xiao 等，2026）则为监督训练筛选经浏览器验证的状态转移。 我们的工作则训练单个智能体策略，通过基于产物的智能体强化学习，在同一不断演进的应用中完成全部四类任务。

sents.zh: 在建模方面，UICopilot（Gui 等，2025b）和 ScreenCoder（Jiang 等，2025）以由粗到细的方式生成代码，JanusCoder（Sun 等，2026）统一了生成与编辑，UI2Code N（Yang 等，2026）和 VisRefiner（Deng 等，2026）基于渲染反馈进行优化，WebWorld（Xiao 等，2026）则为监督训练筛选经浏览器验证的状态转移。

sents.en: Our work instead trains a single policy to compose all four activities within the same evolving application through artifact-grounded agentic reinforcement learning.
sents.zh: 我们的工作则训练单个智能体策略，通过基于产物的智能体强化学习，在同一不断演进的应用中完成全部四类任务。

paragraphs.en: Agentic reinforcement learning optimizes policies through multi-step interactions with tools and environments ( Wang et al., 2025 ; Luo et al., 2025 ) ; SWE-RL ( Wei et al., 2025 ) learns from software evolution data with rule-based rewards, and GiGPO ( Feng et al., 2025 ) combines episode-level advantages with step-level estimates from repeated environment states. In frontend development, WebGen-Agent ( Lu et al., 2026 ) uses screenshot and GUI-agent scores as step-level rewards, ReLook ( Li et al., 2026b ) trains refinement with a multimodal critic, and WebGrader ( Chen et al., 2026 ) derives executable interaction checks from requirements. For trajectories beyond the context window, ReSum ( Wu et al., 2025 ) broadcasts advantages across summarized segments, Context-Folding ( Sun et al., 2025 ) learns branching and folding, and CompactionRL ( Li et al., 2026c ) jointly optimizes execution and summarization. Our approach grounds terminal rewards and intermediate progress estimates in one checklist, redistributes the rollout advantage across segments by changes in these estimates, and trains across context rewrites with message-tree samples and ownership masks.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体化强化学习通过与工具和环境的多步交互来优化策略（Wang et al., 2025；Luo et al., 2025）；SWE-RL（Wei et al., 2025）利用基于规则的奖励从软件演化数据中学习，GiGPO（Feng et al., 2025）将回合级优势与来自重复环境状态的步骤级估计相结合。 在前端开发领域，WebGen-Agent（Lu et al., 2026）使用截图和图形界面智能体评分作为步骤级奖励，ReLook（Li et al., 2026b）借助多模态评论者训练精炼能力，WebGrader（Chen et al., 2026）则从需求中推导出可执行的交互检查。 对于超出上下文窗口的轨迹，ReSum（Wu et al., 2025）将优势跨摘要片段广播，Context-Folding（Sun et al., 2025）学习分支与折叠，CompactionRL（Li et al., 2026c）则联合优化执行与摘要。 我们的方法将终端奖励和中间进展估计都锚定在同一份检查清单上，根据这些估计的变化在各片段间重新分配 rollout 优势，并通过消息树样本和所有权掩码在上下文重写的情况下进行训练。

paragraphs.en: We introduce WebCoder, a general frontend development agent trained with artifact-grounded agentic RL in Webdev-World. A single policy coordinates reproduction, generation, modification, and repair over a persistent project state; one requirement decomposition grounds both terminal rewards and credit assignment across development stages; and compaction with message-tree samples supports training beyond a single context window. On Webdev-Bench, which we introduce to evaluate capability composition, and on Vision2Web, WebCoder improves substantially over its base model and matches or exceeds the strongest proprietary models, supporting artifact evolution under shared requirements as a basis for training general frontend agents.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出 WebCoder，一个在 Webdev-World 中通过以产物为锚点的智能体强化学习训练的通用前端开发智能体。 单一策略在持久的项目状态上协调复现、生成、修改与修复；一个需求分解同时为各开发阶段的终局奖励与信用分配提供依据；结合消息树样本的压缩机制支持超越单一上下文窗口的训练。 在我们为评估能力组合而提出的 Webdev-Bench 以及 Vision2Web 上，WebCoder 相比其基础模型有显著提升，并达到或超越最强的专有模型，从而验证了在共享需求下的产物演化可作为训练通用前端智能体的基础。

paragraphs.en: We used LLM-based coding assistants during this project for code development, data-processing scripts, figure generation, and editing of the manuscript, in the sense described by the ICLR policy. LLMs are also components of the method and the evaluation, and these uses are documented in the paper rather than being incidental: a vision–language judge (GLM-5V-Turbo) forms one leg of the training reward (Section 2.3 , Appendix C.2 ); an LLM acts as the simulated user and the acceptance judge in the Webdev-Bench protocol (GLM-5.3-Flash, Appendix B.2.3 ); LLM-based author, reviewer, and hardening stages assist the construction of Webdev-Bench tasks and hidden checklists, whose outputs were reviewed by the authors (Appendix B.2.2 ); and the official Vision2Web scorer uses LLM judges (Appendix B.1 ). The reliability of the judges is measured in Appendix E and their agreement with human annotators in Appendix H . We did not use LLMs to generate experimental results, fabricate citations, or produce claims without support. The authors reviewed all LLM-assisted text and code and take full responsibility for the content of the paper.

paragraphs.en: This work trains and evaluates agents that write frontend code. Training tasks are constructed from synthetic product specifications and from screenshots of publicly accessible web pages used as visual references; Webdev-Bench tasks are likewise seeded by public-page screenshots, synthetic specifications, or repositories prepared by the authors. No user data, account-restricted content, or non-public documents were collected, and reference pages were selected to avoid personal information. Agents run in isolated containers with no access to external services beyond package registries, and the verifiers inspect only the applications the agents build. Models that reproduce web pages from screenshots could be misused to clone protected designs; our benchmark uses reproduction only as the first step of composite development tasks, and the released materials are intended for research on frontend development agents.
paragraphs.zh: 本工作训练并评估编写前端代码的智能体。 训练任务由合成的产品规格说明以及用作视觉参考的公开可访问网页截图构建而成；Webdev-Bench 任务同样以公开页面截图、合成规格说明或作者准备的代码仓库作为种子。 未收集任何用户数据、账户受限内容或非公开文档，且所选参考页面均避免包含个人信息。 智能体在隔离的容器中运行，除包注册源外无法访问任何外部服务，验证器也只检查智能体构建的应用程序。 能够根据截图复现网页的模型可能被滥用于克隆受保护的设计；我们的基准测试仅将复现作为复合开发任务的第一步，且发布的材料旨在用于前端开发智能体的研究。

paragraphs.en: The method is specified in Section 2 : the environment, the terminal reward and its checklist decomposition, the credit-assignment computation, and the policy objective. Appendix C gives the implementation details needed to reproduce training: context management and message-tree sample construction with pseudocode (Algorithm 1 ), the evidence, verification method, and weight of each requirement type in the reward, the definition of the intermediate potentials and segment offsets, the rollout infrastructure, and all hyperparameters (Table 3 ). Appendix J reproduces the prompts and skill definitions supplied to the agent, the task-construction prompts, and the acceptance prompt. Appendix B.2 describes the benchmarks, the Webdev-Bench construction pipeline, the evaluation protocol with time budgets and retry rules, the judge models, and the exact scoring formulas; Appendix A lists every baseline and its serving configuration. Every number in the tables and figures is computed programmatically from archived per-task reports and judge outputs by scripts that will be released with the benchmark. Upon acceptance, we will open-source the WebCoder model, the Webdev-Bench benchmark, and the training and evaluation code. Judge stochasticity is controlled by median-of-three grading during training and quantified by repeated acceptance passes in Appendix E .
paragraphs.zh: 该方法在第 2 节中说明：环境、终端奖励及其检查表分解、信用分配计算以及策略目标。 附录 C 给出了复现训练所需的实现细节：包含伪代码的上下文管理与消息树样本构造（算法 1）、每种需求类型在奖励中的证据、验证方法与权重、中间势能与分段偏移的定义、推理基础设施以及所有超参数（表 3）。 附录 J 复现了提供给智能体的提示词与技能定义、任务构造提示词以及验收提示词。 附录 B.2 描述了基准测试、Webdev-Bench 的构建流程、包含时间预算与重试规则的评估协议、评审模型以及精确的评分公式；附录 A 列出了每个基线及其服务配置。 表格和图中的每个数字都是由随基准测试一同发布的脚本，从归档的每任务报告和评审输出中以编程方式计算得出的。 验收通过后，我们将开源 WebCoder 模型、Webdev-Bench 基准测试以及训练与评估代码。 评审的随机性在训练期间通过三次取中位数的评分方式加以控制，并在附录 E 中通过重复验收测试进行量化。

paragraphs.en: Vision2Web ( He et al., 2026 ) is a benchmark for evaluating multimodal coding agents on website development, covering static webpages, interactive frontends, and full-stack websites. We evaluate on the Interactive Frontend level (L2), which contains 66 tasks. Each task provides multiple UI prototypes, textual requirements, and supporting assets, and requires an interactive frontend with visual consistency and coherent navigation across pages. This level assesses both visual reproduction and functional implementation, aligning with our focus on frontend development.

paragraphs.en: We allow two hours of development per task and independently deploy and evaluate the resulting projects. During deployment, the project’s startup script is executed in a fresh container, and the application is checked for accessibility at the designated address. Once deployment succeeds, evaluators interact with the application according to predefined workflows, checking functional outcomes and collecting page screenshots. Functional evaluation uses Claude Sonnet 4.6 with playwright-cli to execute interactions and record test-case outcomes. Visual evaluation uses GLM-4.6V ( Z.ai, 2026a ) to compare the captured screenshots against the reference prototypes. The same evaluation configuration is used for all models.

paragraphs.en: We report Visual Score (VS), Functional Score (FS), their average (Avg), and Deployment Success Rate (DSR). These metrics jointly characterize deployability, visual fidelity, and functional correctness.

paragraphs.en: Webdev-Bench evaluates an agent’s ability to develop a real front-end project continuously. The benchmark comprises 40 tasks spanning three starting conditions: replicating a page from a reference screenshot, building an application from a textual product description, and continuing development on an existing repository, including defect repair. Every task is a composite task: four to five natural-language development requirements are revealed one round at a time, and the agent completes them sequentially within a single session on a single project. Each requirement exercises one concrete development operation (replication, data wiring, interaction, layout restructuring, re-theming, and so on), and together they form one sustained, multi-requirement delivery. After all requirements have been revealed and development ends, the final application undergoes a single terminal acceptance pass that re-examines not only the last requirement but the behavior promised by every earlier one. The central question the benchmark asks is therefore explicit: can the agent satisfy each newly revealed requirement while preserving the behavior the project has already established? Figure 6 summarizes the construction and evaluation pipeline; the following subsections cover task composition (§ B.2.1 ), construction (§ B.2.2 ), the evaluation protocol and metrics (§ B.2.3 ), and two representative tasks (§ B.2.4 ).

paragraphs.en: During construction, each requirement is further decomposed into checklist items: observable, operationally verifiable descriptions of application behavior, each annotated with its parent requirement, an evaluation dimension (functional, interaction, visual, or coverage), a weight (1.5 for core items, 1.0 otherwise), and an acceptance criterion. The items are hidden from the agent under evaluation throughout; we refer to them collectively as the hidden checklist. Requirement counts and item counts measure scale at two different levels: one requirement typically constrains page content, functional results, and interaction states simultaneously, unfolding into roughly six items on average. Each task carries 22–33 items, and the full benchmark carries 1,125 (Figure 7 b): 408 functional, 309 visual, 299 interaction, and 108 coverage items (plus one data-consistency item). Coverage items explicitly test whether behavior delivered for earlier requirements still holds after later modifications, realizing the “preserve established behavior” objective at the acceptance level. In sum, the task level characterizes sustained development through progressively revealed requirements, while the acceptance level concretizes those requirements into individually checkable application behaviors.
paragraphs.zh: 在构建过程中，每条需求会进一步分解为检查项：即可观察、可操作性验证的应用行为描述，每项都标注其父需求、评估维度（功能、交互、视觉或覆盖）、权重（核心项为 1.5，其他为 1.0）以及验收标准。 这些检查项在被评估的智能体面前全程隐藏；我们将它们统称为隐藏检查清单。 需求数量和检查项数量在两个不同层面衡量规模：一条需求通常同时约束页面内容、功能结果和交互状态，平均会展开为大约六个检查项。 每个任务包含 22–33 个检查项，整个基准共包含 1,125 个（图 7 b）：其中功能项 408 个、视觉项 309 个、交互项 299 个、覆盖项 108 个（另有一个数据一致性检查项）。 覆盖项显式地测试为早期需求交付的行为在后续修改后是否仍然成立，从而在验收层面实现“保持已有行为”的目标。 总之，任务层面通过逐步揭示的需求刻画持续开发过程，而验收层面则将这些需求具体化为可逐一检查的应用行为。

paragraphs.en: Tasks and their hidden checklists are produced jointly by one pipeline, so that requirement text and acceptance criteria correspond item by item. Construction starts from a specification that fixes a task’s starting condition, operation sequence, and difficulty tier (15 regular, 25 challenge), controlling the composition of the exam at the source. Seed material is then drawn from a curated pool according to the specification: replication tasks receive a full-page screenshot of a real website, and existing-project tasks receive a runnable repository; text-requirement tasks need no external seed. The specification and seed are given to an author agent , which drafts the round-by-round natural-language requirements together with the matching hidden checklist; a reviewer agent reads the draft independently and returns revision suggestions concerning feasibility, ambiguity, and acceptance blind spots, which the author incorporates. The purpose of the two-agent loop is to couple “how a user would phrase the next request” with “what acceptance should later check.”

paragraphs.en: The protocol deliberately separates two roles: driving development forward and producing the final score. Development proceeds in rounds. When requirement j j is revealed, the agent continues working in the same session on the same project, with all later requirements still unknown. At the end of a round, the harness first performs a mechanical health check—launching the application with the task’s own script, probing the service port, and collecting a full-page screenshot, the page text, and console output. A simulated user (GLM-5.3-Flash ( Z.ai, 2026b ) , an LLM independent of the agent) then judges, from this evidence alone, whether the checklist items of the current requirement appear satisfied and issues a pass-or-return verdict with a short critique in the user’s voice that must not quote the items: a pass reveals the next requirement, while a return sends the agent back to rework the current one, with at most three attempts per requirement. All rounds share a time budget proportional to the number of requirements (1,200 seconds per requirement), with gating and feedback overhead charged against it. This gate exists to push development forward in a manner close to a real user; it never sees the hidden checklist and produces no score.
paragraphs.zh: 该协议有意区分两种角色：推动开发前进与产出最终评分。 开发按轮次进行。 当需求 j j 被揭示时，智能体在同一个会话中继续开发同一个项目，而所有后续需求仍然未知。 在一轮结束时，评测框架首先执行一次机械的健康检查——用任务自带的脚本启动应用，探测服务端口，并收集整页截图、页面文本和控制台输出。 随后，一个模拟用户（GLM-5.3-Flash ( Z.ai, 2026b )，一个独立于智能体的大语言模型）仅根据这些证据判断当前需求的检查清单项是否看起来已满足，并以用户的口吻给出简短评述，给出通过或退回的裁定，且评述不得引用检查清单项：通过则揭示下一个需求，退回则让智能体返工当前需求，每个需求最多三次尝试。 所有轮次共享一个与需求数量成正比的时间预算（每个需求 1,200 秒），门控与反馈的开销也计入其中。 该门控的存在是为了以接近真实用户的方式推动开发前进；它从不接触隐藏的检查清单，也不产出任何评分。

paragraphs.en: All scores come from terminal acceptance. After development ends, an acceptance agent (also GLM-5.3-Flash) independent of the simulated user operates the delivered application in a browser and grades every item of every requirement against the hidden checklist on a 0–3 scale; requirements already passed by the gate during development are re-examined all the same. Aggregation follows a per-requirement conjunctive rule: a requirement counts as satisfied only if all items under it reach the top grade, and the per-task satisfaction fraction, macro-averaged over the 40 tasks, is the requirement satisfaction score (RS). Restricting the same grade records to the items of each dimension yields the functional (FS), interaction (IS), and visual (VS) scores; the delivery success rate (DSR) is the fraction of tasks that deliver a runnable application within budget, with all items of undelivered tasks graded 0. The two halves of the protocol thus map exactly onto the objective stated in § B.2 : round-by-round feedback drives new requirements toward completion, while the terminal full re-examination checks whether later modifications broke earlier results.
paragraphs.zh: 所有分数均来自终局验收。 开发结束后，一个独立于模拟用户的验收智能体（同样为 GLM-5.3-Flash）在浏览器中操作交付的应用程序，并依据隐藏清单对每项需求的每个条目按 0–3 分制打分；开发期间已通过门控的需求同样会被重新审查。 聚合采用按需求维度的合取规则：只有某需求下的所有条目都达到最高分，该需求才算满足；按任务计算的满足比例在 40 个任务上做宏平均，即为需求满足分（RS）。 将同样的打分记录限制到各维度的条目上，即得到功能分（FS）、交互分（IS）和视觉分（VS）；交付成功率（DSR）指在预算内交付可运行应用程序的任务占比，未交付任务的所有条目均记 0 分。 该协议的两个阶段因此恰好对应 § B.2 中陈述的目标：逐轮反馈推动新需求走向完成，而终局的全面重审则检验后续修改是否破坏了先前成果。

paragraphs.en: The only initial material is a full-page screenshot of a consulting-firm website, and four requirements are revealed in order (Figure 8 a–b): R1 replicates the landing page from the screenshot; R2 converts the static services section into a bookable expert-session schedule with city and topic filters, a seats-only toggle, sorting, and seat counts that decrement on booking; R3 removes the first-screen privacy-consent overlay and the featured-projects section; R4 re-themes the whole site from deep blue to dark green with warm sand-gold accents on a cream background. The requirements depend on one another: the R2 schedule is built on the layout replicated in R1, and the R4 re-theme must also cover the interactive section newly added by R2. The matching hidden checklist goes beyond “the section exists” (Figure 8 c): a functional item under R2 requires that “with no filters the schedule lists 45 sessions, 8 per page over 6 pages, dropping to 39 sessions over 5 pages when the seats-only toggle is on,” and an interaction item requires that “booking three named sessions in sequence yields a subtotal of £740 with the correct discount applied”—both verifying post-interaction application state rather than the mere presence of controls. A coverage item under R3 requires that no title, body text, or button of the overlay survives anywhere on the page, turning “remove” into a criterion that can be checked verbatim.

paragraphs.en: This section describes how we support development trajectories beyond the context window and construct training samples from them. During rollout, context management allows the agent to continue development within a bounded window. For training, we select samples from the recorded conversation histories, handle their length limits, and determine which generated tokens contribute to the loss in each sample. We describe these steps below and summarize the procedure in Algorithm 1 .
paragraphs.zh: 本节介绍我们如何支持超越上下文窗口的开发轨迹，并从中构建训练样本。 在 rollout 过程中，上下文管理使智能体能够在有限窗口内继续开发。 在训练方面，我们从记录的对话历史中选取样本，处理其长度限制，并确定每个样本中哪些生成的 token 参与损失计算。 我们在下面描述这些步骤，并在算法 1 中总结该流程。

sents.en: This section describes how we support development trajectories beyond the context window and construct training samples from them.
sents.zh: 本节介绍我们如何支持超越上下文窗口的开发轨迹，并从中构建训练样本。

sents.en: During rollout, context management allows the agent to continue development within a bounded window.
sents.zh: 在 rollout 过程中，上下文管理使智能体能够在有限窗口内继续开发。

sents.en: For training, we select samples from the recorded conversation histories, handle their length limits, and determine which generated tokens contribute to the loss in each sample.
sents.zh: 在训练方面，我们从记录的对话历史中选取样本，处理其长度限制，并确定每个样本中哪些生成的 token 参与损失计算。

sents.en: We describe these steps below and summarize the procedure in Algorithm 1 .
sents.zh: 我们在下面描述这些步骤，并在算法 1 中总结该流程。

paragraphs.en: As tool calls accumulate, the conversation history grows. We control its length by applying individual tool-output truncation, historical tool-result folding, and summary compaction in sequence. After compaction, the agent continues from the shortened history while the project files remain in the environment. Figure 10 a illustrates this process in one rollout: prompt length increases as interactions accumulate and decreases when the context is reduced.
paragraphs.zh: 随着工具调用不断累积，对话历史会不断增长。 我们通过依次应用单项工具输出截断、历史工具结果折叠和摘要压缩来控制其长度。 压缩后，智能体从缩短的历史继续运行，而项目文件仍保留在环境中。 图 10a 在一次 rollout 中展示了这一过程：提示词长度随交互累积而增加，在上下文被缩减时则减少。

sents.en: As tool calls accumulate, the conversation history grows.
sents.zh: 随着工具调用不断累积，对话历史会不断增长。

sents.en: We control its length by applying individual tool-output truncation, historical tool-result folding, and summary compaction in sequence.
sents.zh: 我们通过依次应用单项工具输出截断、历史工具结果折叠和摘要压缩来控制其长度。

sents.en: After compaction, the agent continues from the shortened history while the project files remain in the environment.
sents.zh: 压缩后，智能体从缩短的历史继续运行，而项目文件仍保留在环境中。

sents.en: Figure 10 a illustrates this process in one rollout: prompt length increases as interactions accumulate and decreases when the context is reduced.
sents.zh: 图 10a 在一次 rollout 中展示了这一过程：提示词长度随交互累积而增加，在上下文被缩减时则减少。

paragraphs.en: We record the conversation in a message tree to preserve histories before and after context rewrites. Shared messages form a common prefix, while rewritten contexts form separate branches. As illustrated in Figure 11 , the history before compaction remains available, and subsequent responses extend the branch containing the compacted context. Each root-to-leaf path provides a candidate training sequence containing the responses along that path and their context.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将对话记录在消息树中，以保留上下文重写前后的历史。 共享的消息构成公共前缀，而被重写的上下文则构成各自的分支。 如图 11 所示，压缩前的历史仍然可用，后续的回复则延伸包含压缩后上下文的分支。 每条从根到叶的路径都提供了一个候选训练序列，其中包含该路径上的回复及其上下文。

paragraphs.en: To limit training cost, we retain at most K max K_{\max} candidate paths from each rollout. We always retain the initial and terminal candidates, then select the remaining candidates according to measured increases in artifact potential. Figure 10 b shows an example in which six of 34 candidate paths are retained. The curve shows the recorded artifact potential, and the orange markers indicate the selected candidates.
paragraphs.zh: 为了限制训练成本，我们从每次 rollout 中最多保留 K_{\max} 条候选路径。 我们始终保留初始与终止候选，然后根据测得的工件势增量选取其余候选。 图 10 b 展示了一个示例，其中 34 条候选路径中有 6 条被保留。 该曲线显示了记录的工件势，橙色标记表示被选中的候选。

paragraphs.en: This section specifies the verifiers used during training and the credit-assignment computation, complementing Section 2.3 and Algorithm 1 .
paragraphs.zh: 本节规定了训练过程中使用的验证器以及信用分配计算，作为第 2.3 节和算法 1 的补充。

paragraphs.en: The verifier builds the project, resolves its entry point, and renders it in a browser; the product of these three gates is G ∈ { 0 , 1 } G\in\{0,1\} . The quality term combines a deterministic leg and a vision–language judge leg (GLM-5V-Turbo ( Hong et al., 2026 ) ), R = G ⋅ ( 0.6 ​ f det + 0.4 ​ f vlm ) R=G\cdot(0.6\,f_{\mathrm{det}}+0.4\,f_{\mathrm{vlm}}) , with a penalty of 0.1 0.1 when the wall-clock budget is exhausted. Table 2 lists, for each requirement type, the evidence the verifier collects, how it is verified, and its weight. paragraphs.en: We collect 1,556 rollout sessions from Stage 1 (steps 1–14) to characterize the trajectory scale of long-horizon web development. Because context compaction rewrites the interaction history, per-turn token counts alone do not determine the exact length of the full deduplicated transcript. We therefore summarize session scale using the proxy L = max t ⁡ P t + ∑ t O t L=\max_{t}P_{t}+\sum_{t}O_{t} , where P t P_{t} and O t O_{t} denote the prompt and completion token counts at interaction turn t t , respectively. The median L L is 364k tokens, the 90th percentile is 903k, and the maximum reaches 2.02M. As shown in Figure 12 a, 97.9% of sessions exceed the 64k training window under this measure. This mismatch is also evident without the prompt-length term: cumulative generated tokens alone, ∑ t O t \sum_{t}O_{t} , exceed the window in 94.5% of sessions. These statistics motivate context management and the construction of multiple training samples from each long rollout.
paragraphs.zh: 我们从第 1 阶段（步骤 1–14）收集了 1,556 个 rollout 会话，用以刻画长程网页开发的轨迹规模。 由于上下文压缩会重写交互历史，仅凭每轮的 token 数无法确定完整去重转录文本的确切长度。 因此，我们使用代理量 L = max t ⁡ P t + ∑ t O t L=\max_{t}P_{t}+\sum_{t}O_{t} 来总结会话规模，其中 P t P_{t} 和 O t O_{t} 分别表示交互第 t t 轮的提示 token 数和补全 token 数。 L L 的中位数为 36.4 万 token，第 90 百分位为 90.3 万，最大值达到 202 万。 如图 12 a 所示，在该度量下，97.9% 的会话超出了 64k 的训练窗口。 即使不计提示长度项，这种不匹配也很明显：仅累计生成的 token 数 ∑ t O t \sum_{t}O_{t} 就在 94.5% 的会话中超出该窗口。 这些统计结果说明了上下文管理的必要性，以及从每个长 rollout 构建多个训练样本的合理性。

paragraphs.en: Two model-based verifiers are used in this work. The reward judge scores the final artifact of every rollout during reinforcement learning and forms the vision–language-model leg of the terminal reward. The acceptance judge operates the running application at the end of each Webdev-Bench session and assigns every item of a hidden checklist an integer grade from 0 0 to 3 3 , with 3 3 denoting full satisfaction. This appendix measures the repeated-grading error of both and shows, on concrete cases, that their scores correspond to visible differences in the artifacts. Notation follows Appendix B.2.3 : a requirement counts as satisfied only when all of its items receive grade 3 3 , and the mean over requirements is the requirement satisfaction score (RS); restricting items to the function-and-coverage, interaction, and visual dimensions gives FS, IS, and VS.
paragraphs.zh: 本工作使用了两个基于模型的验证器。 奖励裁判在强化学习过程中为每次 rollout 的最终产物打分，构成终端奖励中视觉-语言模型的一环。 验收裁判在每个 Webdev-Bench 会话结束时运行该应用程序，并为隐藏清单中的每一项给出从 0 0 到 3 3 的整数评分，其中 3 3 表示完全满足。 本附录测量了二者的重复评分误差，并通过具体案例表明其评分对应于产物中可见的差异。 记号遵循附录 B.2.3：只有当某需求的全部条目均获得 3 3 分时，该需求才计为满足，需求上的平均值即为需求满足分（RS）；将条目限定在功能与覆盖、交互和视觉三个维度，则分别得到 FS、IS 和 VS。

GRPO builds its gradient from relative advantages among rollouts of the same task, so the relevant comparison is the within-group spread. In the Stage 1 training groups themselves (eight rollouts per task; 220 220 groups and 1,280 1{,}280 gate-passing rollouts from steps 1–14), the pooled within-group standard deviation of the reward is 0.078 0.078 , against a judge noise of roughly 0.008 0.008 once propagated through its weight in the reward: genuine within-group differences are about ten times the measurement noise, and the gradient is driven by policy differences rather than grading jitter.

paragraphs.en: For the 77 tasks from six model runs on which three independent terminal acceptance passes were executed and all three per-item outputs parse, we align the three grades of every item, giving 999 item triples; each pass is a separate session in which the judge restarts and operates the application before grading. At the item level, each item is classified by the range of its three grades: identical in all passes, differing by at most one grade, or differing by two or more. At the task level, RS is computed for each pass and compared across the three passes. Figure 15 shows the result: 89.8 % 89.8\% of items receive identical grades in all three passes, 8.8 % 8.8\% differ by one grade, and 1.4 % 1.4\% by two or more. The three passes agree closely at both the item-grade and the task-level RS layer, indicating that the acceptance judge’s grading is stable and reproducible.
paragraphs.zh: 对于来自六次模型运行的 77 个任务，我们执行了三次独立的终端验收评审且所有三个逐项输出均可解析，我们对每个条目的三个评分进行对齐，得到 999 个条目三元组；每次评审都是一个独立的会话，其中评判者先重新启动并操作应用程序，然后再进行评分。 在条目层面，每个条目按其三个评分的区间进行分类：三次评审完全相同、最多相差一个评分，或相差两个及以上。 在任务层面，为每次评审计算 RS，并在三次评审之间进行比较。 图 15 展示了结果：89.8 % 89.8\% 的条目在三次评审中获得完全相同的评分，8.8 % 8.8\% 相差一个评分，1.4 % 1.4\% 相差两个及以上。 三次评审在条目评分和任务层面的 RS 两个层次上都高度一致，表明验收评判者的评分是稳定且可复现的。

paragraphs.en: The three-pass record of one task shows what this agreement looks like in practice (Table 5 ). The task is a store-operations dashboard with four requirements and 22 items, built by Claude Opus 4.8. paragraphs.en: To analyze the development behavior associated with changes in training reward, we collect 1,556 rollouts from Stage 1, steps 1–14, and examine their model-call records, saved conversation histories, and final-artifact evaluations. Based on the reward curve, we divide the analysis into three windows: Early (steps 1–4), Trough (steps 8–11), and Recovery (steps 12–14). The behavioral analysis focuses on replication tasks, where the reward decline is more pronounced. The three windows contain 291, 267, and 181 replication rollouts spanning 30, 27, and 28 tasks, respectively.
paragraphs.zh: 为了分析与训练奖励变化相关的发展行为，我们从 Stage 1 的第 1–14 步收集了 1,556 个 rollout，并检查其模型调用记录、保存的对话历史以及最终产物的评估结果。 基于奖励曲线，我们将分析划分为三个窗口：早期（第 1–4 步）、低谷（第 8–11 步）和恢复（第 12–14 步）。 行为分析聚焦于复现任务，因为奖励下降在这些任务中更为明显。 这三个窗口分别包含 291、267 和 181 个复现类 rollout，覆盖 30、27 和 28 个任务。

paragraphs.en: Figure 17 shows behavioral changes across the three windows for replication tasks. During the trough, the redundant-operation rate rises from 0.24% to 2.45%, while skill invocation falls from 24.1% to 15.7% and webshot invocation from 79.8% to 66.9%. The reward decline thus coincides with a larger fraction of tool calls repeating previous operations and fewer rollouts invoking Skills or webshot. During recovery, the redundant-operation rate decreases to 0.86%, while skill and webshot invocation rise to 20.8% and 78.7%, respectively. All three metrics move toward their early levels, suggesting a partial improvement in development behavior alongside reward recovery, with fewer redundant operations and renewed use of Skills and webshot. We further examine these changes through policy entropy, generated-word frequencies, and an observed operation sequence.
paragraphs.zh: 图17展示了复制任务在三个窗口中的行为变化。 在低谷期，冗余操作率从0.24%上升到2.45%，而技能调用率从24.1%下降到15.7%，webshot调用率从79.8%下降到66.9%。 因此，奖励的下降伴随着更大比例的工具调用重复之前的操作，以及更少的 rollout 调用 Skills 或 webshot。 在恢复期，冗余操作率下降至0.86%，而技能调用率和webshot调用率分别上升至20.8%和78.7%。 这三项指标都向早期水平回归，表明随着奖励恢复，开发行为部分改善，冗余操作减少，Skills 和 webshot 的使用重新增多。 我们进一步通过策略熵、生成词频以及观察到的操作序列来检验这些变化。

paragraphs.en: To examine whether these behavioral changes coincide with changes in the model’s predictive distribution, we analyze policy entropy during training. Entropy is computed over the full vocabulary and averaged over generated tokens in each training batch. As shown in Figure 18 (a), policy entropy decreases from 0.452 nats at step 1 to 0.386 at step 9, then rises to 0.433 at step 14. Lower entropy during the trough reflects more concentrated predictions on the observed contexts and coincides with increased redundant operations. During recovery, entropy rises as redundant operations decrease.
paragraphs.zh: 为了检验这些行为变化是否与模型预测分布的变化相吻合，我们分析训练过程中的策略熵。 熵是在完整词表上计算，并在每个训练批次中生成的词元上取平均。 如图 18 (a) 所示，策略熵从第 1 步的 0.452 nats 降至第 9 步的 0.386，随后在第 14 步升至 0.433。 谷值期间较低的熵反映了预测在所观察到的上下文上更加集中，并与冗余操作的增多相吻合。 在恢复阶段，随着冗余操作减少，熵随之上升。

paragraphs.en: The evaluation policy is requirement-driven: for every requirement the annotator checks whether the required content is present, whether functional results are consistent with the specification, and whether interaction state is visibly evidenced; visual fidelity and overall usability are considered only afterwards. A deliverable that fails to start loses outright, and a tie is reserved for pairs that satisfy essentially the same requirements with no clear visual gap.

paragraphs.en: Figure 23 gives the full c22 trajectory summarised in the main text. The starting repository is the single-page website of SEDA. Requirement one repairs three dead PRIMER entries so that they scroll smoothly to their target block like the other links. Requirement two removes the investor row and the fundraising figure, tightens the hero from 1085 1085 to at most 900 900 pixels, and redistributes the remaining statistics. Requirement three compacts the five staggered “Why SEDA” parts into two rows of three and two within 1400 1400 pixels while keeping every text and image. Requirement four adds a newsroom of 48 48 articles in five categories with per-category counts on the filter buttons, two sort orders, nine articles per page with pagination and a page indicator, and a read-later mark with a counter and an empty-state message. Requirement five adds a Newsroom entry to the navigation that scrolls to the section and resets category and page while preserving the marks, and replaces one statistics cell with the article count. The simulated-user gate, which judges the current requirement’s checklist items from the running page without revealing them, returns the feedback reproduced under the figure after the first attempt at requirement three: the five parts are still in the old layout and exceed the height budget. The second attempt rearranges them into two rows and passes. The other four rounds pass at the first attempt, and the terminal acceptance grades all 27 27 checklist items 3 3 . The trajectory shows the intended division of labour between the two verifiers: the gate drives development with natural-language feedback and the terminal acceptance checks every item on the finished application.
